Lindemans Chemicals Appoints New Managing Director to Lead Belgian Operations

Lindemans Chemicals announced on Thursday that Dirk Maes has been appointed Managing Director of its Belgian operations, effective July 1. Maes, who brings more than two decades of experience in the European chemicals industry, succeeds Sabine Leclercq, who will retire at the end of June after eight years at the helm.

The board of Lindemans Chemicals cited Maes’s “proven track record in operational excellence and strategic growth” as key factors in his appointment. Prior to joining Lindemans, Maes served as Chief Operations Officer at Veridian Polymers, another major player in the Belgian chemicals sector.

Commenting on his new role, Maes said, “Belgium remains a cornerstone of European chemical manufacturing, and I am honored to take on this leadership role at a time of significant opportunity. My focus will be on driving innovation, ensuring safety, and enhancing sustainability across our Belgian sites.”

Industry analysts welcomed the move, noting that Lindemans has consistently invested in its Belgian operations, which employ over 1,200 people across three sites in Flanders and Wallonia. “Dirk Maes’s extensive knowledge of local and European regulatory environments will be a strong asset as the industry navigates evolving environmental standards,” said Marianne Dupuis, senior analyst at Benelux Chemicals Insight.

The Belgian chemical sector is one of the largest in Europe, accounting for 17% of the country’s industrial turnover according to the Federation of Belgian Chemical Industries (FEBECI). The sector has seen steady growth in recent years, with exports reaching €50 billion in 2023.

Outgoing director Leclercq expressed confidence in her successor. “Dirk’s commitment to sustainable growth aligns perfectly with Lindemans’s values. I am certain the company will continue to thrive under his guidance,” she said in a statement.

Trade union representatives also welcomed the appointment. “We look forward to a constructive relationship with Mr. Maes, particularly as we work together on workforce development and safety initiatives,” said Jan Peeters, spokesperson for the General Federation of Belgian Workers (ABVV).

Lindemans Chemicals confirmed that a formal handover process is underway and that Maes will be introduced to staff at a series of town hall meetings next month.
